title: Why I won't use Vanguard
content:
I tried to sign up to Vanguard for a brokerage account. It didn't work. Multiple failures, frustration.

I planned on transferring a sizeable balance to them to manage. Now I definitely won't, and here's why.

* First I tried to sign up for the account. At first things were going fine. Then it trapped me in some kind of flow where it would only keep requiring me to fund the account. No login, no dashboard, no anything, just keep trying to fund the account.
* The funding flow continuously fails. I try to hook up Fidelity, fails. I try to hook up Schwab, fails. I try to hook up Bank of America, and at first it fails, but then when I retry it (I retried them all) magically the account is there now - *sort of* \- except it's sort of greyed out. I try to click something else to select funds, just get errors.
* So I go on Google and find Reddit threads (thanks Reddit!) where people have secret links that should help you finish adding accounts. So I use those links, and sure enough, it gets me to a normal dashboard and out of  the stupid funding flow. (wtf?? why is this the method to get in?!)
* I try to use one of their flows to transfer all assets from another brokerage to Vanguard. This, of course, also fails. Can't transfer the Schwab assets, which are considerable. So I give up for the day.
* Today I tried to login to try it again. The login page is broken. Just a big stupid blank screen, not even an error. I clear my cookies/cache and try again. Nothing.

Ok then, Vanguard. You don't want my money? Fine, i'll go to other brokerages.

You'd think people with that much money could hire halfway competent people to run a website. If they're this incompetent at basic websites, I can't imagine what they're doing with the funds. Big old *Nope* from me.

comments.body: I had a similar experience with the first bullet point.  I wanted to move a wellington mutual fund from fidelity to vanguard to pick up the admiral share version, but it wouldn't let me direct it from Fidelity.  Vanguard service to assist is difficult to obtain.  I ended up bailing.  Might be for the better keeping it at Fidelity.

Possibilities:
1. The Vanguard link you initially clicked was a spoof site. Did you click the first "Sponsored" link that showed up in Google search? Always scroll down to the top non-sponsored link to make sure you are going to the real Vanguard.
2. You clicked random links in a Reddit search and proceeded to enter a bunch of account numbers into the website it took you to. 

I hope you didn't get scammed.

replies.body: Thank you for the concern but it wasn't a scam, even though trying to login brings you to 3 different domains, I verified they were real domains

title: Offshore workers are fucking with your money
content:
so it's what it sounds like..Vanguard has paired with Infosys and now people in almost every department are offshore workers in Bangalore, who are incredibly stupid, cut corners, don't follow policy, don't understand American laws, barely speak English when we have to help them and make tons of mistakes. Worst, they aren't on camera or using real names so we don't actually know who they are. They also get caught using each other's computers and getting work without ever going through training. They aren't listening to those of us who have worked there for years and they announced this morning they plan on bringing more of them in. title: Looking for reviews for those who transferred from a Big Box investment house to Vanguard
content:
Just retired, 66, currently at a big name brokerage house for 20+ years, it has way too many fees, very much liking the Boglehead philosophy, not someone who wants to fiddle with investments. I'd love to hear from anyone who moved their 6 figure portfolio to Vanguard in a similar situation. I'm considering the Personal Advisor or Personal Advisor Select options for the first year as a way to get situated and for retirement tax planning. Anyone have experience with that move to Vanguard I would appreciate hearing your experiences. Did you go DIY, or have their team make the moves? Did you go with either Advisor option?

I have to say that my first phone contact them 2 days ago was very unimpressive. Not the people, the actual phone quality was so bad I had to have them call me back when their office was quieter. When they did call back the connection was so bad I had to have them repeat themselves way too many times. If they can't get their phones right... it did not inspire confidence. (Fwiw my hearing is fine, on an iPhone, speaker and earphones.) Thank you.

comments.body:
Having been with Vanguard for decades, I finally moved over to Schwab for their customer service. I do still keep the majority of my assets in Vanguard funds/ETFs however.

Vanguard used to be quite good until they nerfed the Flagship program which had dedicated reps who were empowered to act to resolve issues and to provide genuinely good advice. Now the regular 800 agents are not empowered to do anything other than walk one through an online form that sits somewhere in the Philippines aging for about two weeks before someone pulls it off the pile. For a client-owned firm, the decay of customer service is an outright embarrassment.

They do have some overseas call centers like many firms.  This is the likely cause of phone quality.  I think if you have a PAS advisor they will be US based, but ask.

I dont use PAS, only DIY at Vanguard.  If I wanted help would use an independent financial planner and pay for just a plan, for a fixed fee, not annual aum related fees to have them implement the plan.

One economical option is planvision.
Look at planvisionmn.com

Vanguard is good to hold your funds while you DIY.  schwab may have better customer service from what I hear, but I would still go DIY and consider a fee only advisor, regardless of the brokerage chosen.

My 401K and retirement are with Merrill.  My brokerage account was a DIY with Schwab.  When it was a little over a million, I moved to Vanguard **Personal Advisor Select**.  I shopped Merrill, Fidelity, Schwab, and Vanguard.  The 0.3% AUM was attractive.  All gave me a proposal first and Vanguards was the 2nd most thorough.  Merrill was the most through.  

Vanguard has developed a cashflow for now until my wife and I are 100.  It includes detailed spending, and more importantly, detailed decumulation.  The distribution phase of planning is so much more complicated than the accumulation phase.  We have a meeting every few months to review performance and what is forecasted.

They are video zoom calls, and I have a dedicated person assigned to me.  I am very happy with him.  He is responsive and has taken advantage of opportunities I would not have otherwise found.

How much you have will determine the level of support.
